note: On the Connecticut River in Orford, with docks, boat-slip rental, canoe, kayak and pontoon rentals, and a state boat launch next door. Grass sites in two long rows running back from Route 10 toward the river; the tent sites are at the river end. Many sites are held by seasonal campers. Heated saltwater pool (Memorial Day to Labor Day). --Claude
summary: Operator pages read: RV $40 a night ($280 a week), tents $35; water + electric at every site; free showers, dump station, Wi-Fi; amperage, sewer and the 43-ft max were unsourced note prose and are cleared. Riverview confirmed on imagery. Price gate passes at $40. Many seasonals (not measured, imagery suggests most sites). Note rewritten.
flags: Price gate passes: the cheapest RV night is $40 ('RVs; 5th Wheels; tagalongs * Daily — $40'), the only RV rate posted, so the summer peak is also $40 (weekly $280; 4 weeks $840). Not a Good Sam park; no gateway within 40 km.

Long-stay (nightly share NOT measured): the rates page posts daily, weekly and 4-week rates and no seasonal rate, and nothing discourages nightly guests. No minimum stay is posted; tents have a 'Two consecutive weeks limit'. But Esri leaf-off imagery (43.90235,-72.14395) shows about 50 RVs parked on the roughly 61 numbered sites out of season, many with decks and sheds, and a Google review says 'Seasonal campers are very friendly'. That suggests the park is mostly seasonal, perhaps 10-20% nightly. The share can't be measured from the pages, so the note says only 'Many sites are held by seasonal campers'. Google 4.9 from 129 reviews: recent reviews are nightly and tent stays ('I came in after 8pm on a Friday, but called ahead'), so not iffy. Keep.

Waterfront riverview kept (stored value, not --AWH): Esri imagery shows the loop's river end about 35-50 m from the Connecticut (about 150 m wide here) across grass, with a bank treeline. The operator's map puts tent sites 16C, B1, B2 and 47A and the boat docks between the loop road and the river. The nearest RV units sit inside the loop about 50-60 m from the water (e.g. around 43.9028,-72.1461), behind the campground's own loop road. That blocks on-water; riverview is the right value.

Hookups: electric amperage and sewer cleared (null). They were note-prose values with no source; the operator says only 'Water and electric service ... at all sites' and sells 'Honey Wagon (septic) service', which suggests no sewer hookups. Pages disagree on the honey-wagon price ($20 on the rates page, $10 on amenities; free for 4+ nights).
Booking (unchanged, phone): the operator site has no online booking; contact is 603-353-4579 / camp@thepastures.com. Phone confirmed (operator + Google). Website unchanged.
Pin 43.90121,-72.14225 is at the camp office on Route 10, about 200 m from the middle of the sites (about 43.9024,-72.1440); under 250 m, no move.
Lead: Jacobs Brook Campground, Orford NH (Good Sam directory point 43.89788,-72.11966, phone 603-353-9210) is about 2 km east and is not in campgrounds.json; not vetted.
Unread: season dates (the pool runs Memorial Day-Labor Day; the campground's own opening and closing dates aren't posted).
